title: Feature Request: New alarm type for make benefit of a peaceful night's sleep.
symptom: Dexcom users trying to extend sensor life are woken by high and low alarms that fire on a hair trigger when small amounts of sensor noise creep into glucose readings, causing sleep deprivation.
cause: Sensor noise creeps into glucose readings and triggers alarms on a hair trigger, even when settings intended to avoid false alarms are used.
fix: Widen the thresholds of the pre and main low alarms (to 4.0 and 3.6 respectively) and switch back to phone as collector from SW3 on OB1G5; these changes were reported to make the low alert behave correctly.
evidence_quote: OK I did two things and my low alert just behaved correctly. I widened the threshold of my pre and main low alarms (4.0 and 3.6 respectively). Secondly I switched back to phone as collector, from my SW3 on OB1G5.
